stages.title: SUBORDINATE ENRICHMENT — ONLY AFTER THE COMPLETE CORE

pills.text: EARLY COMPANY POLICY OFTEN SOUGHT BUFFERS, BUT AFTER BENGAL
INCREASINGLY USED WAR, DIPLOMACY, RESIDENTS AND SUBSIDIES TO DOMINATE
WELLESLEY'S SUBSIDIARY ALLIANCE TRANSFORMED RULERS INTO DEPENDENT ALLIES
TROOPS, PAID SUBSIDIES, ACCEPTED A RESIDENT AND SURRENDERED INDEPENDENT
INDIAN RULERS SURVIVED FORMALLY, BUT SOVEREIGNTY SHIFTED TO THE

groups.heading: OPTIONAL SOURCE DEPTH
items: Early Company policy often sought buffers, but after Bengal the Company
increasingly used war, diplomacy, Residents and subsidies to dominate Indian states.
Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance transformed rulers into dependent allies: they hosted British
troops, paid subsidies, accepted a Resident and surrendered independent external relations.

groups.heading: ADVANCED DEBATE
items: CAUTION: This produced indirect rule : Indian rulers survived formally, but sovereignty shifted to the Company.
Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse moved from indirect control to annexation by denying adoption rights in selected states.
Awadh's annexation in 1856 used the separate justification of alleged misgovernance, showing that British expansion used multiple legal pretexts.
Mysore under Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan resisted through military reform, diplomacy and attempts to balance British power.

groups.heading: LEGACY / NUANCE
items: Maratha weakness lay in confederate rivalries; British diplomacy exploited divisions among the Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, Bhonsle and Gaekwad.
Sikh power was consolidated under Ranjit Singh, but after his death court
factionalism and military tensions enabled British victory in the Anglo-Sikh wars.
CAUTION: Bengal revenues, sepoy armies and superior logistics allowed the Company to fight repeated wars far beyond its original coastal bases.
